source.label: NASA Space Math, The Mathematics of Ion Rocket Engines, page 64, Problem 1; https://spacemath.gsfc.nasa.gov/weekly/5Page64.pdf
source.question: What will be the speed of the atom, in kilometers/hour, if the voltage grid of the ion engine is 1,300 volts?

givens: NASA page 64 Problem 1: singly charged xenon ion, mass 2.2e-25 kg and charge +1.6e-19 C
NASA page 64 Problem 1: kinetic energy 0.5 m v^2, energy gain q times 1300-V potential drop
NASA page 64 Problem 2 separately supplies grid separation 0.7 mm; used only to instantiate the explicit trajectory
assumptions: Ion initially at rest before entering the acceleration gap; NASA wording does not fully specify the inlet speed
The grid is represented as a fixed prescribed uniform electric field over the gap and the ion is an independent nonrelativistic test particle
Only the particle flight within the grid gap is modeled; no charge cloud, collision, fringe field, source backreaction, or magnetic force
illustrative_choices: Choose positive x axis from injection to exit, launch at (0,0,0) m, x=0.0007 m exit, and potential reference zero at injection
Choose 21 evenly spaced saved samples including the exit crossing instant
Compute native sample exit time from the explicitly recorded prescribed-field assumptions; this is authored inverse algebra, not solved by native engine
Native speed is m/s; the original question requests km/hour, which requires an explicit separate 3.6 unit conversion
This is a public source-derived NON-BLIND rehearsal: the NASA PDF includes an answer key; the PDF bytes and independent provider identity are not authenticated by this local lock

requested_measurements.quantity: speed at the grid exit, native SI value before conversion to requested km/hour
